anomalies.observed: The net named POT merges the fan connector power pin (J2.2), the potentiometer wiper (J3.2), the switched-VCC load node from Q1 drain and jumper JP1, and the MCU analog pins U2.2/U3.2. Thus the fan supply/switched-VCC node is not separated from the potentiometer/MCU analog input.
anomalies.expected: For a standard 4-pin fan controller, the fan power pin and the switched VCC load from Q1/JP1 should be on a separate fan-power net, while the potentiometer wiper and MCU analog input should remain isolated from that power node (or be properly divided/clamped). A 4-pin fan pin 2 should be a stable supply or isolated load, not the potentiometer setpoint signal.

evidence.quote: POT : J2.2(Pin_2,passive) J3.2(Pin_2,passive) JP1.1(A,passive) Q1.3(D,passive) U2.2(XTAL1/PB3,bidirectional) U3.2(PB3,bidirectional)
VCC : C1.1(passive) J5.2(Pin_2,passive) JP1.2(B,passive) Q1.2(S,passive) R1.1(passive) R6.1(passive) U1.3(VI,power_in)

anomalies.impact: If Q1 turns on or JP1 is closed, VCC (likely above 5 V, since U1 is a 5 V regulator) is applied directly to the potentiometer wiper and MCU PB3. This can damage the MCU/potentiometer, load the analog setpoint with the fan supply, and make the fan power/control behavior differ from the intended fan controller.

parsed.summary: The main suspicious deviation is that the POT net combines the fan connector power pin and switched-VCC load with the potentiometer wiper and MCU analog input; this merges a power/load node with an analog control node and is not supported by standard fan-controller design practice.
